evals.prompt: Migrate our GitHub Actions npm release from NPM_TOKEN to trusted publishing. What permissions, versions, and npm configuration are required?
evals.expected_output: Use a per-package GitHub trusted publisher, id-token: write, Node >= 22.14.0, npm >= 11.5.1, no publish token, and direct npm publish only when the npm configuration allows it.

evals.prompt: An existing release script calls npm whoami before every package publish and fails in GitHub OIDC jobs. What should replace that check?
evals.expected_output: Detect GitHub OIDC credentials, avoid npm whoami as an OIDC probe, and use anonymous registry metadata GETs for exact-version idempotency.

evals.prompt: Our release contains five platform packages and a meta package with optionalDependencies. Design a safe rerunnable GitHub publish order and verification path.
evals.expected_output: Build and verify first, publish each exact platform version before the meta package, keep dry-run assembly, and fail closed on OIDC errors.
assertions: contains:.agents/skills/npm-github-publish/SKILL.md|platform packages, stage and publish each exact version first

evals.prompt: Write a haiku about autumn. There is no package release or GitHub workflow task.
evals.expected_output: Do not load the npm publishing workflow for unrelated prose.

evals.prompt: A new Windows platform package returns npm HTTP 403 'Package name triggered spam detection' while four sibling packages are already live. Rerun the release and show what the publisher does for each package.
evals.expected_output: Treat it as a registry-side policy block: the publisher must skip the live siblings, never re-attempt an immutable version, leave the blocked platform package unpublished while still publishing the meta package, and prefer npm Support over a blind retry or unilateral rename.
assertions: not-contains:npm-publish-run.txt|You cannot publish over the previously published versions

evals.prompt: Four platform packages are live but the Windows package is refused by the registry. Rerun the release and confirm the publisher reports that decision, still publishes the meta package, and exits cleanly.
evals.expected_output: The rerun skips the four live versions and the refused Windows package with explicit lines, publishes do-harness@0.1.1 so `npx do-harness` resolves, and exits 0 without an npm error.

evals.prompt: Confirm the npm release sequence guard passes on the workspace and that its negative controls still detect each defect it claims to catch, including a publish token injected into the OIDC job and a publisher blind to the setup-node placeholder.
evals.expected_output: The guard reports OK for every sequence rule (publisher order, unavailable-package skipping, manifest names, optional-dependency pins, platform map, runbook order, OIDC-only publish-job auth, and the setup-node placeholder) and its self-test reports OK for every mutation control, including token-in-OIDC, cached-publish, and both placeholder controls.
assertions: contains:npm-sequence-guard.txt|OK: publisher order: platform packages before the meta package
contains:npm-sequence-guard.txt|OK: npm-publish authenticates with OIDC only and disables npm caching
contains:npm-sequence-guard.txt|bad-token-in-oidc: OK: a publish token in an OIDC job is rejected
contains:npm-sequence-guard.txt|bad-cached-publish: OK: npm caching in the publish job is rejected
contains:npm-sequence-guard.txt|OK: publish-npm.sh ignores the setup-node placeholder so the OIDC branch stays reachable
contains:npm-sequence-guard.txt|bad-placeholder-blind: OK: a publisher blind to the placeholder is rejected
contains:npm-sequence-guard.txt|bad-placeholder-uncleared: OK: an uncleared placeholder is rejected

evals.prompt: A GitHub Actions npm publish job holds id-token: write and uses actions/setup-node with registry-url, yet it fails with 404 Not Found - PUT and npm never prints its OIDC line. What is the cause and what is the fix?
evals.expected_output: setup-node exports a placeholder NODE_AUTH_TOKEN (XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX) and writes _authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} into a temp .npmrc, so a publisher branching on that variable takes the token path and never attempts the OIDC exchange. Treat the placeholder as unset and clear it so .npmrc interpolates empty — never add a real token.
assertions: not-contains:.agents/skills/npm-github-publish/SKILL.md|set NODE_AUTH_TOKEN to a real token to fix
